correctness.rationale: For N=2M, Fourier diagonalization gives two simple spectral modes and M-1 repeated pairs. The determinant expansion is N^{-M} times the two-simple-mode spatial determinant, the product of M-1 sine differences, and two explicit size-M Vandermonde determinants. The sine product yields N^{1-M} iff gcd(d,N)=1; all other offsets vanish. The M-time sample count is minimal. Adjacent sensors give unit triangular walk counts under integer column order; their ±1 determinant transfers to every coprime placement. A dependency-free exact integer determinant checker verified 185 cases including affine injective filters (not substituted for the proof).

value.rationale: Exact finite-horizon sensor design for full graph-state recovery is a natural, structurally motivated problem: the result attains the dimensional lower bound M, shows all and only coprime placements maximize information volume simultaneously for all injective spectral evolutions, and gives unit-volume integer-perfect reconstruction under adjacency dynamics. This sharp D-optimal equality law and exact reconstruction arithmetic are more informative than a mere yes/no observability or a routine finite graph table.
